summary: Loaigen CEO Park Sung-ki’s series argues that humanoid and service robots cannot rely on “physical AI” alone, because real-world behavior also depends on modeling invisible social context: norms, appropriateness, and judgments that are not captured cleanly in sensor data. This fourth installment frames robot intelligence as a combination of physical and social world models, shifting the question from whether a robot can execute an action to whether it can choose an action that makes sense in human environments.

title: Video Friday: Albatross Falls, Spins, Self-Rights, and Sails Away
summary: ALBATROSS is a hybrid aerial–marine robot that can be dropped from the air, autorotate down without a parachute, self-right on the water, and then use the same rigid wings as sails for autonomous wind-powered travel. The clever part is the mechanical reuse: one passive wing structure handles descent, landing recovery, and marine propulsion, pointing toward deployable ocean-sensing platforms that can arrive quickly and then operate for long periods with very little energy.

extra.full_text: Video Friday is your weekly selection of awesome robotics videos, collected by your friends at IEEE Spectrum robotics. We also post a weekly calendar of upcoming robotics events for the next few months. Please send us your events for inclusion. CoRL 2026 : 9–12 November 2026, AUSTIN Humanoids 2026 : 6–9 December 2026, SANTA CLARA, CA Enjoy today’s videos! We’ve developed ALBATROSS, a hybrid aerial–marine robot that can be released from the air, autorotate down to the water without a parachute, passively self-right after landing, and then reuse the same rigid wings as sails for autonomous wind-powered navigation. The key idea is to make the physical structures do as much of the work as possible. Rather than carrying separate systems for aerial descent, landing, and marine propulsion, ALBATROSS uses the same wings for both autorotation and sailing, with minimal actuation. Ultimately, we’re interested in whether platforms like this could combine rapid aerial deployment with persistent, energy-efficient marine sensing. title: 로소타, TIPS 선정…수술 술기 데이터 수집·표준화 기술 개발
summary: Rosota, a surgical-data AI robotics startup, was selected for Korea’s 2026 TIPS R&D general track to develop technology for collecting and standardizing surgical technique data for a Surgical Robotics Foundation Model. The project matters because high-quality, structured operative motion and skill data are a bottleneck for training generalizable robot-surgery AI systems, and TIPS support gives the company funding and validation to push that infrastructure forward.

extra.full_text: 수술 데이터 기반 AI 로보틱스 기업 로소타(Rosota, 대표 서예찬)가 중소벤처기업부의 ‘2026년 팁스(TIPS) R&D 일반트랙’에 최종 선정됐다고 2일 밝혔다.‘팁스(TIPS)’는 민간투자와 정부 지원을 연계해 유망 기업을 육성하는 대표적인 창업 지원 프로그램이다. 민간 운영사가 기업을 발굴해 투자·추천하면 정부가 연구개발 자금 등을 지원하는 방식으로 운영된다.로소타가 선정된 이번 과제는 ‘서지컬 로보틱스 파운데이션 모델(Surgical Robotics Foundation Model) 학습을 위한 수술 술기 데이터 수집·표

title: THG Fulfil expands distribution partnership with AutoStore
summary: THG Fulfil is expanding its AutoStore distribution partnership so it can sell AutoStore warehouse automation systems not only through its Robotics-as-a-Service model but also via traditional CapEx ownership. The move gives customers more flexibility in how they adopt AutoStore’s robotic storage and retrieval systems, potentially broadening uptake among fulfilment operators with different financing preferences.

extra.full_text: THG Fulfil, the fulfilment operating system from THG Ingenuity, has announced the expansion of its distribution partnership with AutoStore. The agreement enables THG Fulfil to offer AutoStore systems through both traditional CapEx ownership and its existing Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model. title: Aseon CEO: ‘The opportunity is to make vehicle servicing as autonomous as driving’
summary: Aseon is tackling the less glamorous bottleneck in robotaxi operations: making depots that can autonomously charge, clean, inspect, and ready driverless vehicles without human attendants. The pitch is that robotaxi fleets will not scale just by removing drivers from the road; they also need service infrastructure that can keep vehicles cycling through maintenance and back into use with the same level of automation.

extra.full_text: The robotaxi industry has spent billions of dollars developing vehicles that can drive without a human behind the wheel. title: We built this factory twice — once in the digital world, once for real. 💻➡️🏭
summary: UBTECH says it used an industrial digital-twin simulation to build and validate a factory virtually before constructing the physical version. The system checked layout, logistics, and production rhythm ahead of time, pointing to a smart-manufacturing workflow where humanoid-robot production can be debugged and optimized before equipment is installed.

title: T1’s overseas debut, hands-on experiences, and firsthand feedback at IROS 2026
summary: Astribot is taking its T1 humanoid robot overseas for the first time at IROS 2026, showing hands-on demos and gathering feedback from researchers and partners. The company is positioning T1, priced from US$18,000, as a robot that improves through use, with early exploration across logistics, retail, bartending, and lab operations.

extra.full_text: Beyond the show, discover how Astribot and our partners are exploring new possibilities across logistics, retail, bartending, and laboratory operations. T1 from US$18,000. AI That Grows by Doing.
